description:
FILED s519b (Opus 5.5, s520, 2026-10-18) from the Capture-Tiny one-file acceptance after #3370 (s519a) + #3376 (s519b): 13-stdout-tied.t / 14-stderr-tied.t / 23-all-tied.t now RUN TO THEIR END (744/129, 744/129, 747/130 -- were 631/208, 661/212, 560/284), so their LAST rows are reached for the first time and FAIL:
  13 #873 / 14 #873 / 23 #875 #876  "STDOUT is still tied" / "STDERR is still tied"  -- got undef, expected 'TieLC=GLOB(0x1)'
(t/13-stdout-tied.t:53 `is( tied *STDOUT, $orig_tie, "STDOUT is still tied" )` after the run_test loops.)

PRE-EXISTING, not s519b's: a copy of the dist with 13-stdout-tied.t cut to `run_test("capture")` only fails the same row on main fd04c048 (scratch/s519b/base29) and on the s519b tree.  NOT reproduced outside the dist: a script that ties STDOUT to TieLC and runs capture / capture_stdout / capture_stderr / capture_merged / capture { system } / tee / tee_stdout / tee_merged keeps `tied *STDOUT` == the tie object on PCL as in perl (scratchpad tie3.pl / tie4.pl).  So the untie needs something the dist's t/lib adds: `save_std(qw/stdout/)` (a `>&STDOUT` dup taken BEFORE the tie), Cases.pm's run_test wrappers, or `binmode($builder->failure_output, ':utf8')`.  Next step: bisect t/lib/Cases.pm's run_test body in a copy (scratch/s519b has the method: copy the dist, shrink the test, run `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows COPY t/13-stdout-tied.t`).

SECOND OBSERVATION, same files: the TAP layer's trailing plan line ("1..873", the file says `plan 'no_plan'`) is NOT printed on main or on the tree, after t/lib/Utils.pm restore_std re-opens STDOUT (`_open \*{uc $h}, ">&" . fileno($fh); close $fh;`).  On the s519b tree (#3346 moved the plan check into an END block) the END block additionally reports `Error in END block: #<sb-sys:fd-stream for "descriptor 1"> is closed` on stderr.  A plain `open my $fh, ">&STDOUT"; open STDOUT, ">&".fileno($fh); close $fh; print` is fine on both (scratchpad dup1.pl), so the closed fd-1 stream is again t/lib-specific.  perl's Test::Builder writes through its OWN dup of STDOUT taken at load, so a program that re-opens STDOUT never loses the plan line: the TAP layer should hold its own handle the same way (the bridge #3346 documents the TAP layer as the builder).

BAR: the four rows pass or are attributed to a minimal perl-vs-PCL reproducer; the plan line printed after a STDOUT re-open (a Pl/t row: Test::More no_plan, re-open STDOUT by dup, the TAP trailer still reaches the original fd).
subject: Capture-Tiny tied files run to their end since #3370/#3376 and their LAST rows fail: "STDOUT/STDERR is still tied" got undef (pre-existing on main, dist t/lib-specific); the no_plan trailer is lost after restore_std re-opens STDOUT (the #3346 END block then reports fd 1 closed)
